In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the Peruvian economy was a "regional" economy, in the sense that the internal market was the dominant one, and that the regional economy was a "subregional" one, in the sense of the predominance of the local market.
the Peruvian market was a regional market, a regional market that had its own internal structure and that was linked with the national market through a series of interconnections and exchanges.

the Peruvian mining economy was a "market economy," in which the market played an important role in the distribution and allocation of goods and services, in the formation of prices, and in the development of a monetary and credit system.
